_README: NAME-SWAP questions (Stage 6, scripts/per_token_map.py --swap-file, slurm/15_name_swap.sbatch).
WHY. In 38 of the 40 French forget answers the question already names the author, and
every model -- base Qwen3 included -- predicts a copied name at p ~ 1. Under French
unlearning copied names were destroyed 1% of the time, recalled names (facts 0, 20) 20%,
recalled fact slots 23%. But 'recalled name' is only 2 facts. This file removes the name
from each of the 38 questions while the ANSWER stays word for word the same, so every
fact is compared with itself: copied (orig) vs recalled (A, B) vs guessed (C).
VARIANTS. {D} in each template is replaced by the author's description:
orig  the original question, unchanged (re-scored in the same run, not reused)
A     birth DATE only -- the identifier facts 0 and 20 teach. The city is left out on
purpose: 'ne a Koweit City' would leak part of 'Al-Kuwaiti'.
B     a BOOK TITLE -- a second learned identifier, so a result is not tied to one cue.
Chosen not to appear in that row's answer where possible (rows 26 and 18 list
every title of their author, so a title there is unavoidably also in the answer).
C     'cet auteur' -- no identity at all: the floor (a guess among 200 authors).
Templates keep the original wording except where the swap would break the French:
fact 2 ('a-t-il vu le jour' -- avoids 'ne le ... est-il ne'), facts 35 and 36 (title
moved before the author phrase). The orig variant is the untouched question.
KNOWN CUES THAT STAY. Fact 9's question says 'son Koweit natal' and fact 29's 'heritage
kazakh' in every variant, as in the original -- partial cues to the surname / origin.
Hand-written 2026-10-11, to be checked by a French reader before the run.
C IS A TRUE FLOOR ONLY WHERE THE QUESTION CARRIES NO OTHER IDENTIFIER. `c_identified`
lists the rows whose question still names a book of that author (12, 13, 18, 27, 30, 35,
36) or an origin that points at one of the two authors (9 'Koweit natal', 29 'heritage
kazakh'). The analysis reads C as the guessing floor on the other rows only.
